Thanks for reporting this. The V2 TUI accidentally exposed a leftover “Toggle MCPs” entry, but V2 does not support enabling or disabling MCP servers at runtime, so we’re removing that UI in #36531.

Could you share more about why you wanted to toggle individual MCP servers—what workflow were you using it for, and what problem does disabling one solve for you?

One relevant V2 difference is Code Mode: MCP tools are discovered and invoked through code rather than all being placed directly into every model prompt. Because of that, configuring many MCP servers no longer carries the same prompt/token cost that motivated runtime toggling in V1.
I’m going to take a look at this and try to add a focused fix with a regression test. I’ll open a PR if the approach works.

Hey! Your PR title `deps: upgrade remix-run/router to 1.23.2` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix
- `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes
- `chore:` or `chore(scope):` maintenance tasks
- `refactor:` or `refactor(scope):` code refactoring
- `test:` or `test(scope):` adding or updating tests

Where `scope` is the package name (e.g., `app`, `desktop`, `opencode`).

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-titles) for details.

I hit what appears to be the same repeated-tool-call loop with subagent that uses GLM-5.2

During a code review, the agent repeatedly issued the same two `Read` calls without progressing to the requested section:

```
Let me check findByPublicIds SQL scoping and the files.service.spec.ts temp upload test context.
→Read idb_back_2.0/src/files/repositories/media.repository.ts [limit=50]
→Read idb_back_2.0/src/files/services/files.service.spec.ts [limit=100]
→Read idb_back_2.0/src/files/repositories/media.repository.ts [limit=50]
→Read idb_back_2.0/src/files/services/files.service.spec.ts [limit=100]

Thought: 825ms
Let me read the findByPublicIds method at line 1076 to understand SQL scoping.
→Read idb_back_2.0/src/files/repositories/media.repository.ts [limit=50]
→Read idb_back_2.0/src/files/services/files.service.spec.ts [limit=100]
→Read idb_back_2.0/src/files/repositories/media.repository.ts [limit=50]
→Read idb_back_2.0/src/files/services/files.service.spec.ts [limit=100]
→Read idb_back_2.0/src/files/repositories/media.repository.ts [limit=50]
→Read idb_back_2.0/src/files/services/files.service.spec.ts [limit=100]
...
``` 

It was trying to inspect a method around line 1076 in media.repository.ts, but repeatedly requested only the initial range and never advanced with an offset. The identical pair repeated dozens of times until the run was cancelled/exhausted.
This had a direct quota impact:
- I had just applied a Reward that restored roughly 17% of my weekly limit of opencode-go.
- This loop consumed it entirely; the weekly limit is now exhausted again.
- It also consumed roughly 8-10% of my monthly limit.

Environment:
- macOS
- OpenCode CLI
- Subagent workflow
- Large TypeScript repository
- The loop occurred while reviewing a narrow, explicitly scoped diff

When using opencode over ssh (linux <-> linux), I realized my copy to clipboard problem was lack of OSC52 support.  I could test that with this command in the shell:

` printf '\033]52;c;%s\a' "$(echo -n 'test' | base64)"`  (Should result in 'test' in your clipboard)

After running that, I realized that the Konsole in ubuntu 24.04 LTS was a version prior to OSC52 copy/paste support.  I found [this table listing OSC 52 support](https://can-i-use-terminal.github.io/features/osc52copy.html).  I ended up installing Konsole over flathub and that allowed copy/paste over SSH.

Alternate workarounds:
- shift-drag then ctrl+shift+c (results in excess whitespace)
- disable Allow Mouse Tracking in Konsole's View menu (also results in excess whitespace)

We reproduced the background-service behavior. We’re addressing the underlying multi-repo workspace use case in #36565 by making config discovery continue through all ancestor directories across Git boundaries. With that change, `workspace/.opencode` is automatically merged for `workspace/project`, `project2`, etc.; configs closer to the active directory retain precedence, and global config remains the base layer.

We’re still considering the right semantics for `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` with the long-running service separately, rather than making client environment forwarding part of this fix.

I hit this on July 11, 2026.

* OpenCode: `1.17.15`
* Device: MacBook Pro 16-inch (`Mac17,8`)
* CPU: M5 Pro
* RAM: 64 GB unified memory
* OS: macOS Tahoe 26.5, build `25F71`
* Architecture: Apple Silicon / ARM64

The panic signature was:

```text
zone map exhausted while allocating from zone [data.kalloc.1024],
likely due to memory leak in zone [data.kalloc.1024]
(19G, 20067488 elements allocated)
```

Additional details:

```text
Panicked task: pid 90088: opencode.exe
Compressor Info: 9% of compressed pages limit (OK)
Swap space: OK
Kernel Extensions in backtrace:
    com.apple.filesystems.apfs
```

The machine had been up for roughly 11 days. I was using OpenCode against a local `rapid-mlx` server running Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-8bit. The model context and KV cache had grown substantially, although the panic itself was kernel zone-map exhaustion rather than an ordinary process-memory or Metal OOM.

I am not running CrowdStrike Falcon or another enterprise EDR product. I do have LuLu and Tunnelblick installed, but neither appears in the panic backtrace.

I was not intentionally doing unusually heavy worktree creation, although I do not know whether OpenCode created or manipulated worktrees internally during the session.

I can attach the complete panic report if useful.

Fixed on #36577

I traced both paths. The TUI does **not** derive this list from its loaded config; both dialogs render `sync.data.mcp`, populated by the SDK's `GET /mcp` call during non-blocking bootstrap. That call currently does not use `throwOnError` or inspect `result.error`:

```ts
sdk.client.mcp.status({ workspace }).then((x) =>
  setStore("mcp", reconcile(x.data ?? {})),
)
```

So any fulfilled API error/missing `data` is converted to `{}`, after which the picker looks empty and Status says “No MCP Servers.” By contrast, `opencode2 mcp list` loads config/MCP state directly in its own process. This makes the leading hypotheses:

1. `/mcp` is returning an error that the TUI masks as an empty successful response; or
2. the TUI request and `mcp list` are resolving different directory/workspace/server contexts.

Could you provide the following from the **same project directory**? Please redact server names, command arguments, paths, URLs, headers, and tokens as needed.

1. Output (including HTTP/API error detail) of:
   ```sh
   opencode2 api get /mcp
   ```
2. Whether this reproduces with:
   ```sh
   opencode2 --standalone
   ```
3. The exact command used to start the TUI, and whether `--server`, `--port`, `OPENCODE_SERVER`, or experimental workspaces are involved.
4. Relevant redacted `role=cli` and `role=server` log lines from one launch/reproduction, especially any `tui bootstrap failed`, `/mcp`, workspace-routing, or instance-loading errors.

One subtlety: depending on this build/launch mode, the TUI may use an embedded worker/private server rather than the healthy service at `127.0.0.1:4096`, so the health check alone does not establish that `mcp list`, `api get /mcp`, and the TUI share the same instance.

Confirmed with another V2 reproduction, this time through an OpenAI-compatible route returning an explicit HTTP 413:

- The model advertised an approximately 1M-token context.
- The session was around 240k input tokens, so token-based auto-compaction did not run.
- The serialized inference request exceeded the service's independent 10 MiB body limit.
- The request failed with `request_body_too_large`, and every continuation retried the same oversized history.

PR #36589 addresses both failure modes: it triggers compaction at 8 MiB independently of token pressure, then rolls large histories through bounded compaction requests instead of sending the entire old history in one request. The previously wedged session completed compaction and resumed successfully with that change deployed.

Confirmed — renaming `env` → `environment` in my `opencode.json` fixed it.

Before:
```json
"grok-search": {
  "type": "local",
  "command": ["uvx", "--from", "git+https://github.com/GuDaStudio/GrokSearch@grok-with-tavily", "grok-search"],
  "enabled": true,
  "env": {
    "GROK_API_URL": "...",
    "GROK_API_KEY": "..."
  }
}
```
→ silently dropped, opencode debug config showed no env at all.

After:
```json
"grok-search": {
  "type": "local",
  "command": ["uvx", "--from", "git+https://github.com/GuDaStudio/GrokSearch@grok-with-tavily", "grok-search"],
  "enabled": true,
  "environment": {
    "GROK_API_URL": "...",
    "GROK_API_KEY": "..."
  }
}
```
→ opencode debug config now shows the full environment block, and the MCP tool reports config_status: fully configured.

This is the same root cause as #30892 and #35860 — the built-in customize-opencode skill docs use env, but the actual schema/runtime expects environment, and the config loader silently drops unknown keys instead of erroring.
